name: Disorder of Catecholamine Synthesis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Catecholamine Synthesis Disorders

criteria.description: Presence of abnormal levels of catecholamine metabolites (e.g., low homovanillic acid and 3-methoxy-4-hydroxyphenylglycol) in cerebrospinal fluid
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in catecholamine biosynthesis (e.g., TH, DDC, GCH1)
Early onset of neurological symptoms including dystonia, hypotonia, and autonomic dysfunction
Improvement of symptoms with administration of L-DOPA or dopamine agonists

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of biochemical abnormalities and genetic confirmation along with compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: CSF neurotransmitter analysis is critical for diagnosis; genetic testing confirms etiology.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic early-onset progressive dystonia due to dopamine deficiency
searchTerms: muscle contractions due to dopamine deficiency
involuntary muscle spasms related to dopamine

pathognomonic.notes: Generalized low muscle tone affecting motor milestones
searchTerms: low muscle tone and delayed movement
floppy muscles with poor motor skills

pathognomonic.notes: Impaired autonomic regulation leading to blood pressure instability

common.notes: Episodes of sustained upward eye deviation
Poor sucking and swallowing due to neuromuscular impairment
Excessive saliva production related to autonomic dysfunction
Disrupted sleep patterns including insomnia or fragmented sleep

occasional.notes: Occasional epileptic events in some patients
Low blood sugar due to impaired catecholamine regulation
Behavioral changes related to neurotransmitter imbalance
Reflux symptoms secondary to autonomic dysfunction
Peripheral vasoconstriction due to autonomic impairment

rare.notes: Early parkinsonian features in some late-onset cases
searchTerms: movement problems similar to Parkinson's in teens

rare.notes: Unexplained fever episodes possibly related to autonomic instability
Blurred vision or diplopia secondary to neurological involvement

laboratory: Low cerebrospinal fluid homovanillic acid (HVA) and 3-methoxy-4-hydroxyphenylglycol (MHPG)
imaging: Normal brain MRI or mild nonspecific changes
Functional imaging may show reduced dopamine transporter activity
genetic: Pathogenic variants in tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) gene
Variants in aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (DDC) gene
other: Positive clinical response to L-DOPA therapy

distinguishingFeatures: Marked norepinephrine deficiency with elevated dopamine
Improvement with low-dose L-DOPA and absence of severe autonomic symptoms

redFlags: Progressive early-onset dystonia with autonomic instability
Failure to thrive with feeding difficulties in infancy
Lack of response to standard symptomatic therapies without L-DOPA
references: Fitzgerald, K. et al. Disorders of Catecholamine Biosynthesis: Clinical and Molecular Features. Neurology. 2022.
Orphanet Report Series: Disorders of Catecholamine Synthesis. Orphanet. 2023.
Ng, J. et al. Genetic and Biochemical Diagnosis of Catecholamine Synthesis Disorders. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2021.
